title: Human body systems
subject: science
strengths: Most of the class can put digestion in the right order: mouth, then stomach, then intestines.
The class can describe the lungs filling and growing bigger as air flows in, then shrinking as air flows back out.

modelAnswers.question: What happens to the lungs when you breathe in, and what happens when you breathe out?
modelAnswers.answer: The lungs fill with air and grow bigger, then shrink as the air flows back out.

modelAnswers.question: A drop of blood leaves the heart and travels to the body. What happens to that drop next?
modelAnswers.answer: It travels back to the heart and goes round the loop again.

commonErrors.misconception: The heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood.
commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that the heart burns up blood like fuel, so the body must keep making fresh blood.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say what happens to a drop of blood after it leaves the heart and reaches the body.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: the drop travels back to the heart and goes round the loop again; blood is never used up.

commonErrors.misconception: The heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner says the heart can run out of blood because pumping uses it up.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say why the returning blood proves the heart does not use blood up.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: the same blood comes back to the heart to be pushed around again, so the loop never uses the blood up.

nextSteps: Reteach the blood loop, landing that the heart is a pump and the same blood keeps going round instead of being used up.
Practise tracing one drop of blood out to the body and back before answering loop questions.
